title: AI on AWS with Amazon Bedrock
subtitle: Not a better model -- a better procurement and security story

slides.title: What Bedrock actually is
bullets: An AWS-authenticated front door to models you did not train
SigV4 credentials, IAM authorization, CloudTrail audit, no API keys
Model providers cannot see your traffic -- separate deployment accounts
The value is procurement and security, not model quality
Two-person startup? Call the provider directly. Enterprise? This.
slides.notes: Be blunt up front. People arrive expecting Bedrock to be magic; it is plumbing, and the plumbing is the point. Ask the room who has waited six weeks for a third-party data review.

slides.title: Choose X when
rows: one API, one bill, VPC endpoints
Train, fine-tune, serve your own weights
Managed RAG without a vector pipeline
ingest to retrieval as one resource
Full control of chunking and retrieval
managed knobs stop where research starts
slides.notes: The decision rule to say out loud: if the weights are your problem you want SageMaker; if they are someone else's problem you want Bedrock. They are neighbours, not competitors.

slides.title: Two endpoints, and you will meet both
bullets: bedrock-runtime -- InvokeModel, Converse, plus OpenAI/Anthropic-compatible APIs
bedrock-mantle -- Anthropic Messages, OpenAI Responses and Chat Completions
Quotas are tracked SEPARATELY per endpoint, same model
Batch inference and Provisioned Throughput exist on bedrock-runtime only
Model invocation logging captures bedrock-runtime only -- audit accordingly
slides.notes: The logging asymmetry is the one that bites compliance teams. If your audit trail matters, build on an endpoint that can be audited.

slides.title: Converse is the API. Stop writing InvokeModel bodies.
bullets: InvokeModel takes a raw per-provider body -- an adapter per vendor
Converse normalises request AND response across every message model
system is a LIST of blocks, not a string
content is a LIST of ContentBlocks, not a string
Swap models by changing one string, not by rewriting a client
slides.notes: Show the two snippets side by side if you can. The Anthropic body wants anthropic_version; Meta wants a flat prompt. That divergence is what Converse buys you out of.

slides.title: The response envelope -- memorise this
bullets: output.message.content -- list of ContentBlocks
stopReason -- end_turn, max_tokens, tool_use, guardrail_intervened
usage -- inputTokens, outputTokens, totalTokens (+ cache fields)
metrics.latencyMs -- server side, excludes your network
BRANCH ON stopReason. Never on the response text.
slides.notes: The max_tokens case is the silent bug: code that ignores stopReason truncates answers and nobody notices for a month. Make them write the four values down.

slides.title: ConverseStream is a different shape
bullets: messageStart -> [contentBlockStart? delta+ stop] -> messageStop -> metadata
contentBlockStart appears for TOOL USE only
Tool arguments arrive as PARTIAL JSON strings -- accumulate, then parse
usage arrives only in the final metadata event
Needs bedrock:InvokeModelWithResponseStream, a different IAM action
slides.notes: Two production failures here. Abandoning the iterator loses your token accounting. And an IAM policy with only InvokeModel passes every test then 403s on the streaming path in prod.

slides.title: Tool use: the loop you own
bullets: Bedrock never calls your tool -- it returns stopReason tool_use
You execute, then send a toolResult back in a USER message
Echo the toolUseId. Append the ENTIRE assistant message.
One toolResult per toolUse, all in a single user message
On failure return status:'error', not an exception -- let it recover
A one-tool answer costs TWO model calls. Bound the loop.
slides.notes: The user-role rule is the most common ValidationException in the loop. The cost note matters: a five-hop agent is closer to fifteen chat messages because context grows every hop.

slides.title: The tool description IS the prompt
bullets: The model decides from description, not from your function name
Write it as an instruction: 'Use this whenever the user asks...'
inputSchema is JSON Schema under an inputSchema.json wrapper
toolChoice: auto (default) | any | tool -- support varies by model
Tool arguments are untrusted input produced by a model. Validate.
slides.notes: Highest-leverage string in the whole definition. Overlapping descriptions across two tools is how you get a model that picks the wrong one 30% of the time.

slides.title: Inference profiles and the ID that fails
bullets: anthropic.claude-... = foundation model; us./eu./apac./global. = profile
Many newer models are ONLY reachable through a profile
Geographic keeps data in a geography; global is ~10% cheaper
No routing surcharge; priced by the Region you called from
Never hardcode an ID -- run list-foundation-models first
slides.notes: Calling the bare model ID when a profile is required gives a ValidationException that says so, but only if you read it. Also: Anthropic models need a one-time use-case form per account.

slides.title: The cross-Region IAM trap
bullets: Authorization evaluates the profile AND the model in EVERY Region
Source Region plus every candidate destination Region
Grant only the profile and you get intermittent 403s
Use bedrock:InferenceProfileArn so model access is profile-scoped
Region-allowlist SCPs break CRIS without a carve-out
slides.notes: This is exercise 3 in the lab. It works in staging and fails one request in three in production, which is the worst possible failure mode.

slides.title: Knowledge Bases: chunking strategies
rows: you measured and know your docs
long technical docs -- best second try
slides.notes: Hierarchical resolves the Module 08 tension: small embeddings retrieve precisely, large contexts answer well. Warn them it returns fewer results than numberOfResults, because siblings collapse into parents.

slides.title: Retrieve vs RetrieveAndGenerate
bullets: Retrieve: chunks, scores, metadata -- you own the prompt
RetrieveAndGenerate: retrieval plus generation plus citations, one call
Use Retrieve for anything real; R&G is a demo accelerator
Vector stores: OpenSearch Serverless, S3 Vectors, Aurora pgvector, Neptune
OpenSearch gotcha: the index must use faiss, not nmslib
Build your own when chunking is your measured bottleneck
slides.notes: Generation is where the product lives. R&G gives you almost no control over the prompt, reranking, or retrieval-failure handling. Start with S3 Vectors for large corpora and low query volume.

slides.title: Bedrock Agents is in maintenance mode
slides.quote: Amazon Bedrock Agents (now Agents Classic) is no longer open to new customers.
bullets: AgentCore is the replacement: Runtime, Gateway, Memory, Identity, Policy
Framework-agnostic -- LangGraph, CrewAI, Strands, or your own loop
Gateway speaks MCP; Managed Knowledge Bases plug in as tools
AWS stopped selling the loop and started selling the infrastructure
Most Bedrock agent tutorials on the internet are now wrong
slides.notes: Read the quote verbatim from the docs page. This single note invalidates a large fraction of the Bedrock content published before 2026. The strategic read is correct: the loop is where you differentiate.

slides.title: Guardrails -- and the gap in them
bullets: Six policies: content, denied topics, words, PII, grounding, automated reasoning
Attach per request, or call ApplyGuardrail with no model at all
Fires -> stopReason guardrail_intervened, usage all zeros
Guardrails do NOT evaluate toolResult content or tool arguments
One guardContent block means ONLY guardContent gets evaluated
Blocked content is written to invocation logs in plain text
slides.notes: Bullet four is the prompt-injection path in every agentic Bedrock app. If untrusted text arrives via a tool, you must call ApplyGuardrail on it yourself. Cross-reference Module 13.

slides.title: Cost: the levers in the order that pays
bullets: 1. Right-size the model -- beats every other optimisation combined
2. Cache the stable prefix with cachePoint -- free, compounds
3. Bound maxTokens -- output tokens are the expensive ones
4. Move what can wait to batch -- but batch has no tool calling
5. Trim retrieved context before adding hardware
6. Provisioned Throughput LAST, with a month of data
slides.notes: PT is billed hourly whether used or not, commits for up to six months, and does not work with inference profiles. Buying it to fix uncharacterised throttling is a classic expensive mistake.

slides.title: The token accounting trap
bullets: With caching on, inputTokens counts ONLY non-cached tokens
true input = inputTokens + cacheReadInputTokens + cacheWriteInputTokens
Cache checkpoints evaluate tools -> system -> messages, cumulatively
Changing a tool definition invalidates system and message caches
Below the per-model minimum it succeeds and silently does not cache
Verify with cacheReadInputTokens, not with hope
slides.notes: Dashboards built on inputTokens alone show a 60% usage drop the day caching ships, and somebody plans capacity around it. Make them check the response fields.

slides.title: Errors: retry which, never which
slides.notes: Retrying a 400 or a 403 burns quota and never succeeds. That is how a bug becomes an outage. Use botocore mode='standard', not the default 'legacy'.

slides.title: Operations checklist
bullets: botocore Config: standard retries, 6 attempts, read_timeout, tcp_keepalive
VPC endpoints for bedrock-runtime AND bedrock-agent-runtime
Model invocation logging ON -- it is off by default
requestMetadata on every call; tagged application inference profiles
Alarms on InvocationThrottles, p99 latency, token rate, hop count
Write down what happens when us-east-1 is throttled
slides.notes: The 350-second idle timeout on NAT gateways and VPC endpoints needs BOTH tcp_keepalive=True and a lowered kernel tcp_keepalive_time. Either alone does nothing. Close by asking the room the last bullet.
